one_liner: Stripe has a broad, well-documented REST API with self-serve free API keys, OAuth via Stripe Apps/Connect, and an official hosted MCP server.
auth_notes: API uses API keys (sk_/rk_) sent via HTTP Basic (key as username) or bearer. OAuth 2.0 is available for Stripe Apps for multi-user access on behalf of other accounts; public distribution of OAuth apps may require Stripe app review.
access_notes: Creating a Stripe account generates test/sandbox keys immediately; live keys need account setup. Multi-user OAuth via Stripe Apps requires creating an app (public distribution subject to review).
blocker_notes: Users can paste restricted API keys immediately; OAuth for public apps may need Stripe review but is not required to ship.

evidence.quote: The Stripe API authenticates requests using [HTTP Basic Auth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basic_access_authentication). Provide your API key as the basic auth username value.
Use the industry standard OAuth 2.0 to authenticate requests to the Stripe API on behalf of your users.
After you create a Stripe account, we generate two pairs of [API keys](/keys) for you
When you create a RAK in the Stripe Dashboard, you select which Stripe resources the key can access and the permissions for each resource
Stripe hosts a remote MCP server at `https://mcp.stripe.com`. This allows secure MCP client access via OAuth.
